title: How to interpolate between two surveys
text: start loading two example datasets included wbpip. need clean datasets ensure aren’t missing values, welfare values sorted properly.
code: # Load datasets data('md_ABC_2000_income') data('md_ABC_2010_income') # Clean datasets  dl <- list(md_ABC_2000_income, md_ABC_2010_income) dl <- lapply(dl, function(df) {   wbpip:::md_clean_data(df, welfare = 'welfare', weight = 'weight')$data }) #> ℹ Data has been sorted by variable "welfare" #> ℹ 30 NA values in variable "welfare" were dropped #> ℹ Data has been sorted by variable "welfare"

title: How to interpolate between two surveys
text: calculate weighted mean surveys. Note welfare values survey given local currency units add _lcu suffix vector. helpful distinguish values conversions later . survey means might look like large, underlying welfare values reported yearly values. Since international poverty lines reported (international) dollars per day, survey mean also needs converted daily values.
code: # Calculate survey mean (in local currency units) svy_mean_lcu <- vapply(dl, FUN.VALUE = numeric(1), function(df) {   weighted.mean(df$welfare, df$weight) }) print(svy_mean_lcu) #> [1] 3436146 7186782 # Convert to daily values  svy_mean_lcu <- svy_mean_lcu / 365

title: How to interpolate between two surveys
text: order poverty statistics comparable time across countries also need make sure survey means adjusted take different price levels account. can done converting purchasing power parity (PPP) adjusted dollars. thus create new vector, svy_mean_ppp, using function deflate_welfare_mean() adjust values. imagine PPP value 1081, CPI value first survey year 0.6 CPI value second survey year 0.9. CPI based PPP year, meaning PPP exchange rate provided year 2011, CPI value 2011 1 (except cases 2011 saw change currency). gives us daily welfare mean $14.5 2000 welfare mean $20.2 2010.
code: svy_mean_ppp <- deflate_welfare_mean(   welfare_mean = svy_mean_lcu,    ppp = 1081,    cpi = c(0.6, 0.9)) print(svy_mean_ppp) #> [1] 14.51449 20.23827

what: Calculate the predicted mean for the request year
title: How to interpolate between two surveys
text: now almost ready calculate poverty statistics year interested , one final step need conduct first. need predict value daily welfare mean request year (Year availble survey). prediction, national accounts data, e.g. Gross Domestic Product (GDP) Household Final Consumption Expenditure (HFCE), used approximate growth daily welfare mean. Let’s imagine calculating poverty statistics year 2005, using GDP data proxy values. need three GDP values; one first survey year (2000), one second survey year (2010) one request year (2005). see two predicted survey means identical. supplied GDP values moving direction, implying -direction interpolation used compute predicted means.
code: # Predict welfare means for the request year pred_mean_ppp <- predict_request_year_mean(   survey_year = c(2000, 2010),    survey_mean = svy_mean_ppp,   proxy = list(     value0 = 1200, value1 = 1900, req_value = 1500   ) ) print(pred_mean_ppp) #> [1] 16.96754 16.96754

title: How to interpolate between two surveys
text: now information need calculate poverty statistics request year. function fill_gaps() takes following main arguments; request_year: integer value request year. data: list one two country-year datasets. predicted_request_mean : numeric vector predicted mean(s) request year. survey_year: numeric vector survey year(s). addition also need specify type data using (micro grouped) value using poverty line. case supply cleaned datasets, predicted means survey year surveys since want interpolate . also supply 2005 request year, $1.9 poverty line specify data type micro. function returns list different poverty statistics, including estimated welfare mean, headcount, poverty gap poverty severity. code: # Poverty line needs to be expressed in monthly international dollar values # The conversion from daily to monthly values needs to happen at a higher level # in the functions call stack for efficiency purposes poverty_line <- 1.9 * 365 / 12  # default_ppp # This will need to be provided directly by a potential end-users # For production use: This value will be fed directly to the function depending  # on the requested country / year. ppp_value <- 58.16  # requested mean # This is the survey mean in internationl dollars # The conversion from LCU to international dollars needs to happen at a higher  # level in the fucntion call stack for efficiency purposes. # This parameter is also used for interpolation computation to query the welfare # distribution using a different mean. welfare_mean <- 225  out <- wbpip:::md_compute_pip_stats(welfare        = df$welfare,                                     population     = df$weight,                                     povline        = poverty_line,                                     default_ppp    = ppp_value,                                     requested_mean = welfare_mean) out #> $poverty_line #> [1] 57.79167 #>  #> $mean #> [1] 225 #>  #> $median #> [1] 132.9027 #>  #> $headcount #> [1] 0.1418472 #>  #> $poverty_gap #> [1] 0.051882 #>  #> $poverty_severity #> [1] 0.02683585 #>  #> $watts #> [1] 0.07785021 #>  #> $gini #> [1] 0.5147999 #>  #> $mld #> [1] 0.473487 #>  #> $polarization #> [1] 0.469777 #>  #> $deciles #>  [1] 0.01348020 0.02630982 0.03516682 0.04436668 0.05461301 0.06523872 #>  [7] 0.08463966 0.10850619 0.15757546 0.41010343
